title: What Exactly Is Alex Garland’s Civil War?

commenti.body: My concern is that the movie, while it looks good, will play it safe and ignore some of today’s issues for a more palatable version of an actual civil war. Whatever causes the civil war in the movie will be so different from what we’re dealing with now that the movie won’t be relatable and therefore less interesting and thought provoking.
Or you’re missing the point completely. Why does this have to represent real life?

I think Garland already made the action movie he dreamt up as a 12 year old boy, and that movie was DREDD.

Anyway, OP, I'm not sure if you're asking if there's been any more information of what the movie is about, or if you're asking us to speculate along. Because it hasn't really been revealed anywhere at all. We'll just have to see when the movie is out, rather than guessing based on a movie trailer that is obviously going to emphasize the action aspect to sell it.

I can speculate though, given the wild reveal that the uprising involves a surprising alliance of California and Texas, that the movie will touch on immigration since that's the most obvious thing those two states have in common.

Every movie doesn’t have to, but in this specific case I’m assuming the movie will be meant as some type of commentary on some aspect real life, probably something around American politics, so ignoring the cores of the real issues it’s exploring may undercut part of its message/impact.

Maybe Alex Garland just wants to make a mindless action movie and doesn’t want people to think about it past that, but I’d seriously highly doubt that.

By the looks of it, the meat of the film is going to be exploring and speculating how our current divisions could give rise to an alien world. 
“What kind of American are you?” will be a question whose answer could decide your life, or at the very least the degree of suffering you’re about to face either by the militia next door, or by your own government. The “fencesitter” shop owner on the beginning who acts like it’s just everyone else being whipped into a hysteria by the Internet or the news won’t be able to shield themselves with their ignorance for long, because civil war eventually makes its way to every doorstep. I have faith that there will be something more to this, and based on the imagery some wild shit could be in there.

The problem you’re having is you think you’re able to define the real issue. No one can agree on the real issue. Are you left leaning? Then you have an opinion on the cause. Are you right leaning? You have a different opinion. This movie, if going the route you want, would take a hard political stance and that is not something that makes a good film.
I don’t know, the trailer certainly seems to hit on that theme. Civilian casualties from airstrikes, Texas/Cali. rising up …

It doesn’t. I’m just thinking that a movie like this might be more engaging if it does represent real life a little. It might be a little more exciting if you sit there and go “huh, this is plausible.”

My big worry is that they are gonna try and play it down the middle and we’ll end up with something ultimately toothless. 

The scene with Jesse Plemmons asking them what kind of Americans they are gives me hope that this will actually drill down and have something to say about the current political landscape. 

But the fact that they have Texas and California together kind of makes me think they’re gonna try an both sides it which will dilute any potential message the film could have.

I’m able to define the issues I understand, which as an American with a brain and an education means I understand quite a few things pertaining to the ways we could potentially end up in a situation resembling the one in the movie.

It’s pretty clear by aligning Texas and California they’re going for a “both sides” equivocation, which is admittedly necessary for a wide-release mainstream movie, but also belies the fact the one real avenue we have to that path is strictly that of a right wing Christian nationalist variety.

The reason these anxieties in our nation exist are because they’ve been fostered by those elements, so pretending that the potential for an antidemocratic takeover (president unilaterally taking a 3rd term) is some vague notion that could only happen in this abstract fantasy could make the end result feel toothless.

I’ll see the movie because Garland always does interesting stuff, but Men was somehow both heavyhanded and muddled in its messaging, so I don’t have the most faith in his ability to walk this tightrope.
I guess, but he’s still making a movie about a modern American civil war. Not sure how his nation of origin has much to do with the messaging.

You proved my exact point with this post. You understand why it’s important that Texas and California were aligned for the movie, but you’re unhappy because you want it to align with how *you* perceive the current state of the world. This is exactly what he is trying to do. 

I suggest having more of an open mind and realize that everyone that leans heavily on the political spectrum are closer to Jesse Plemons character than they realize.

My thinking is that he is writing from a British perspective. He probably visits the US regularly, but is not fed a daily diet of our media. Essentially he would bring an outsider's perspective, so it might not align with how one of us might imagine an American civil war kicking off or transpiring
